newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-NEW BRAZIL SEASON CLAIMS FIRST COACHING VICTIM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW BRAZIL SEASON CLAIMS FIRST COACHING VICTIM.

text.p: Brazil's new soccer season, which is barely two weeks old, has already claimed its first coaching victim.
Paulo Autuori, formerly of Portuguese club Benfica, took over as coach of Cruzeiro on Friday to replace former international Oscar, who resigned after just one major match in charge.
Oscar was jeered as Cruzeiro lost 2-1 at home to Gremio in a South American Libertadores Cup tie on Wednesday.
At one stage during the game fans chanted the name of his predecessor Levir Culpi. He walked out on the club the next morning.
The turnover of coaches in Brazil is extraordinarily high, even by the standards of a profession which is known to offer almost no job security.
Leading clubs Botafogo, Vasco da Gama, Fluminense, Internacional and Corinthians all employed four different coaches last year in a vain quest for success.
But the most volatile club were Guarani where Beto Zini, famous for trying to interfere in team selection, employed 10 coaches.
